answer: Because the kernel index resolves every citation against the terrace checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the pigment audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 5 times over for the same share of the pool. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
